name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,224

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bizarrely, bolshevized exiles belie perverted rulers such as Stalin

indicators.note: to exile is to send away, so one set of letters is banished from the other word
perverted means twisted out of shape, so the banished letters need not appear in their printed order
anything done bizarrely is done in a strange, disordered way, so what remains is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: the starting stock of letters
taken as written: these five letters are struck out of the longer word

explanation.surface: Exiled anti-Soviet émigrés denounce the twisted despots of the Kremlin.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, E, L, I, E from BOLSHEVIZED, leaving O, S, H, V, Z, D, which rearrange to VOZHDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vozhd is the Russian title for a supreme leader, applied above all to Stalin, so VOZHDS are such rulers.

clue.text: Shrub of superior class planted among old beans, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word before it is dropped
planted among means set down in the middle of, so one letter goes inside another word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
pulse is the collective name for beans, peas and lentils
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A bush of high quality grows in a patch of old bean plants.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and middle-class English usage, so U stands for superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulus is the species name of the guelder rose, a viburnum bush, and Chambers lists it as a plant.

clue.text: Holding better half, win

blocks.note: one's better half is one's spouse
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: Someone clings to their spouse and comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Holding looks like a verb in the surface, but the definition is the noun, a parcel of land held by a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandland was the Scottish term for land held by a husbandman, a tenant farm or smallholding.

clue.text: Fashionable new blue clothes and kid’s tight sweater

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the outer word goes round the others

blocks.note: sky blue; the sky is blue
what is fashionable is in
N is the abbreviation for new
to kid someone is to tease, or rib, them

explanation.surface: A child dressed in a trendy new blue tight-fitting jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes is the verb, meaning dresses, not the noun; kid is a verb too, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinny-rib is a close-fitting ribbed jumper; sweater is a knitted top worn over a shirt.

clue.text: Tool of little weight I had placed in can, briefly

indicators.note: placed in says the first items are set inside the following word
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word before it is dropped

blocks.note: can is slang for a lavatory, as is privy
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a tiny amount of something in a tin for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Can is the American slang for a lavatory, not a tin; the shortened word is split after its first letter to take the insert.
explanation.definitionFit: Pozidriv is a trademarked cross-head screwdriver design, so the word names a workshop implement.

clue.text: Rest on box, maybe, when eyeing up the local crumpet

indicators.note: placed on means coming after, so the first-named piece goes second in the joined string
in a down answer up means read from bottom to top, the opposite of normal

blocks.note: the box is a slang name for television, the tele
a kip is a nap or rest

explanation.surface: A man nods off in front of the TV while ogling the attractive woman next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpet seems to be a leering slang term for an attractive woman; here it is the food, in a regional variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Pikelet is the Midlands and northern English name for a thin crumpet or griddle cake.

clue.text: Village governor clown’s cut short, before magistrate intervenes

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the final letter goes
to intervene is to come between, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a zany is a clown or buffoon
someone up before the magistrate is in court

explanation.surface: A local official who is a buffoon is jailed short-term after appearing before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Clown's is clown is, not a possessive; being up before a magistrate is the British idiom for appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A zupan was the head of a district or village community in historical Slavic lands such as Serbia and Croatia.

clue.text: Hamish’s pet that’s housed in pentagonal structure

blocks.note: first meaning: a Scots word for a sulk, as in to take the pet
second meaning: the US Department of Defense, headquartered in the Pentagon

explanation.walkthrough: Hamish is a typical Scottish name, so Hamish's marks a Scottish word; pet here means a fit of sulking, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a dod is a fit of ill humour, and the American defence ministry's initials are housed in the Pentagon.

clue.text: Displays rapt attention before rival players making introductions

blocks.note: someone showing rapt attention is agog
in bridge East and South sit in opposing partnerships

explanation.surface: A fan watches spellbound as opposing teams are presented to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partners are North-South against East-West, so East and South are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An isagoge is a scholarly introduction to a subject, a preliminary treatise, so the plural means prefaces.

clue.text: Enterprise, possibly akin to corrupt Republican’s introducing Ukrainian

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or debased, so the word beside it is broken up and reformed

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
the Starship Enterprise is the USS Enterprise; possibly flags it as one example of a named ship
the letters of akin, rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked American politician is compared to a business while bringing in someone from Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republican's R comes first, introducing the rest: R + USS + NIAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russniak is a Ruthenian, a member of the Ukrainian-speaking people of the Carpathian region.

clue.text: Leisurely hack once turning in biog and a photo

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
turning means facing the other way, so the concealed letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of biog, all of and and a, and the start of photo

explanation.surface: A journalist, once a hack, is shown in a biography with a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Hack here is a horse for ordinary riding, not a journalist; reading biOG AND A Photo backwards gives PADNAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A padnag is an archaic word for an easy-paced riding horse, a steady ambling hack.

clue.text: States that female at home should frame charcoal drawing

indicators.note: to frame something is to surround it, so the outer letters go round the middle ones

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the United States
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A political demand that a woman staying home should surround herself with art.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusain is the fine charcoal stick used by artists, and also a sketch made with it.

clue.text: Ingredient of perfumes, all blended with no oil

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for scent in which everything is mixed without any oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that a perfume ingredient is made with no oil, when linalool is itself a component of essential oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Linalool is a fragrant alcohol found in lavender and coriander and widely used in scent manufacture.

clue.text: Doing my job for G Lansbury’s successor, dispensing tips for beef producers

indicators.note: dispensing with tips means discarding the very first and very last letters

blocks.note: the setter's job is writing clues
George Lansbury was followed as Labour leader by Clement Attlee, so his initial comes too

explanation.surface: A setter explains clue-writing for the political heir of George Lansbury.
explanation.walkthrough: The G in G Lansbury signals that the successor also comes with an initial: C Attlee. The tips removed are those of the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Luing cattle are a hardy beef breed developed on the Scottish island of Luing, so the herd produces meat.

clue.text: Girl in Oz, along with French cardinal, were stripped: one posed for minister there

indicators.note: stripped means with the outer layer taken off, so only the inner letters stay

blocks.note: Dorothy Gale is the heroine of The Wizard of Oz
a cardinal number in French: ten
the inside of were

explanation.surface: Dorothy from Oz and a French churchman are both undressed in a strange tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is both the Wizard's land and Australia; there in the definition points back to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian parliament a Dorothy Dixer is a friendly question planted by a government backbencher for a minister to answer.

clue.text: Shouting that has nasty Yogi bear breaking sick Cindy’s heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
nasty suggests something turned bad, so the letters are thrown out of order
breaking means smashing up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the middle letter of Cindy

explanation.surface: Cartoon character Yogi Bear upsets his girlfriend Cindy Bear by being nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Yogi Bear and Cindy Bear are a cartoon couple, so bear just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoicks is the huntsman's cry urging on hounds, and yoicksing is giving that halloo, a kind of hunting cry.

clue.text: Junior Civil Service raised with us periodically pressing hazard in S America

indicators.note: pressing means squeezing in, so letters are pushed between the others
periodically means at regular intervals, so the inserted letters recur throughout
in a down answer raised means lifted to read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Jr is the abbreviation for junior
CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
us read as the plural of the letter U, one placed before each letter

explanation.surface: A junior civil servant is promoted while we periodically lobby about a South American danger.
explanation.walkthrough: Us is the plural of U, and a U goes in front of each of J, R, C and S before the whole is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucuruju is a Brazilian name for the anaconda, a huge snake that is a danger in South American rivers.

clue.text: I’m thinking a note well employed to stop crying game

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these letters are pushed into the following word

blocks.note: um is the sound someone makes while pondering
taken as written
NB is nota bene, Latin for note well
howling is loud crying

explanation.surface: Someone pausing to note something useful in order to stop a baby crying.
explanation.walkthrough: Note well looks like an instruction to the reader, but it is one unit, the Latin abbreviation; the insert goes in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Human bowling is a novelty pastime in which a person, often inside a ball, is rolled at skittles.

clue.text: NZ fish: last two removed from store

indicators.note: removing the last two means the final pair of letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: a warehouse is a storage building

explanation.surface: A New Zealand fish is taken out of storage after the last two go.
explanation.definitionFit: The warehou is a New Zealand sea fish, a type of trevalla, named from the Maori word for it.

clue.text: African capital in role of spouse of pop artist

blocks.note: acting as means in the role of
pop is father, and his spouse is mother, or ma
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A city plays the part of the wife of a pop artist like Warhol.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop artist reads as one phrase but splits: pop is Dad, and artist stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Asmara is the capital city of Eritrea, in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Particular local tobacco Greek lad oddly neglected to bring back

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a particular, fussy person in dialect

indicators.note: neglecting the odd positions leaves only the even-placed letters
bring back means return to the start, so the kept letters run backwards

blocks.note: a quid is a plug of chewing tobacco
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A fussy villager has a Greek boy fetch his tobacco, oddly forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiddler is a dialect word for a fussy, pernickety person, someone over-particular about trifles.

clue.text: Triumphant expression in the case of Labour landslide

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside shell, its first and last letters
in says the first item sits inside the shell that follows

blocks.note: the outside letters of Labour
aha is a cry of triumph

explanation.surface: A party cheers when Labour wins an election by a landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: Landslide sounds like an electoral victory in the surface, but the definition is a literal earth movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A lahar is a mudflow of volcanic debris and water sweeping down a volcano's flanks, a kind of slip.

clue.text: Sikh and what he wears five of: article impressing prince

indicators.note: impressing means pressing into, so one item is pushed inside another

blocks.note: the five Ks are articles of faith a baptised Sikh wears, each beginning with K
Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A description of a Sikh, his five articles of faith, and royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: HAL is pressed inside the two Ks letters, and the article A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Khalsa is the order of initiated Sikhs, and the word is also applied to an individual member.

clue.text: By virtue of being German I can present cup at St Andrews?

blocks.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of
ich is German for I

explanation.surface: A German golfer claims the right to hand over the trophy at the home of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrews, the Scottish golfing town, stands for Scotland as a whole, and the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaich is a shallow two-handled Scottish drinking bowl, often given as a trophy or welcome cup.

clue.text: One’s grazed in places: wound, superficially, not wide

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a pasture, in regional use

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for the word after it

blocks.note: to wing someone is to wound them slightly
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Someone was grazed in a few spots: a shallow wound, not a broad one.
explanation.walkthrough: Grazed suggests a skin wound, but it means eaten by livestock; a wide in cricket is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Ing is a northern English dialect word for a meadow, especially low riverside pasture where animals feed.

clue.text: Shaft for lifting ring, say, with buckles

indicators.note: something that buckles is bent out of shape, so the letters are pushed into a new order

blocks.note: O is ring-shaped
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ring is used to lift something until it bends under the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoistway is the vertical well in a building through which a lift or hoist travels.

clue.text: Peak summer months, good to go west, saving for after vacation

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good moves leftward, from the end of its word to the front
vacating a word empties it, leaving just its first and last letters
saving means keeping safe inside, so one piece is held within the others

blocks.note: the abbreviations for two summer months
the outside letters of for

explanation.surface: A summer holiday plan: head west in good time, putting money aside for afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second month's G moves to its front, west being leftward in an across answer, and the emptied word then sits between that G and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a famous mountain in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland, so it is a summit.

clue.text: Muse, wasting time on couple I must follow and trap in room

indicators.note: wasting means throwing away, so a letter is lost from the word it follows

blocks.note: the two letters of the alphabet that come immediately before I
Erato is the Muse of love poetry
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A poet broods, wasting time on a relationship he must pursue.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse looks like the verb to ponder, but it is one of the nine Muses; couple means a pair of alphabet letters, the two just before I.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherao, from Hindi, is a protest where workers confine an employer to an office until demands are met.
